title: Etale patching on a scheme infinitesimal pushout
statement: Let $T\to T^+$ be a thickening of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-closed-immersion], meaning a closed immersion inducing a homeomorphism, and let $T\to S$ be affine, meaning that inverse images of affine opens are affine. Put $P=S\amalg_T T^+$ [lem-sfb-scheme-affine-thickening-pushout]. An etale triple is a pair of etale scheme morphisms $X\to S$, $Y\to T^+$ [def-weil-etale-morphism] with an isomorphism $\phi:X\times_S T\simeq Y\times_{T^+}T$ [def-pc-fibre-product]; its morphisms are pairs commuting with $\phi$. The pullback functor from etale schemes over $P$ to etale triples is an equivalence. A quasi-inverse sends a triple to the scheme pushout $X\amalg_{X\times_S T}Y$ with its induced map to $P$, which is etale. The equivalence has its canonical unit: the two projection-induced maps from $X$ and $Y$ to the respective base changes of this pushout are isomorphisms compatible with $\phi$. Its canonical counit says that every etale scheme $W\to P$ is the pushout of $W\times_P S$ and $W\times_P T^+$ along $W\times_P T$. No quasi-compactness, separation or finite-order assumption is imposed.

proof.text: Base change preserves etale morphisms by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-scheme-base-change], so the displayed pullback assignment defines $F$ on etale schemes; the common $T$-pullbacks are identified by their projections [def-pc-fibre-product]. For an etale triple set $U=X\times_ST$ and identify it with $Y\times_{T^+}T$ via $\phi$. Apply [lem-sfb-infinitesimal-pushout-affine-charts] to obtain the scheme pushout $Z=X\amalg_UY$ and its induced map $Z\to P$. The node applies to arbitrary schemes over the two pieces and does not require etaleness or flatness.

proof.text: For a morphism of triples $(a:X\to X_1,b:Y\to Y_1)$, compatibility with $\phi$ makes the two maps into $Z_1$ agree on $U$. The pushout universal property [lem-sfb-scheme-affine-thickening-pushout] gives a unique map $Z\to Z_1$ over $P$; uniqueness proves identity and composition laws. More explicitly, a map $Z\to W$ over $P$ is precisely a pair $X\to W$, $Y\to W$ over $P$ agreeing on $U$. The fibre-product universal property [def-pc-fibre-product] identifies this pair with a morphism of triples to $F(W)$: its components are the unique pairs $(X\to W,X\to S)$ and $(Y\to W,Y\to T^+)$. Projecting these pairs back to $W$ reverses the construction. These operations commute with composition, giving the natural adjunction $G\dashv F$ once $Z\to P$ is shown etale.

source.place: Tags 07RV (lemma-equivalence-categories-schemes-over-pushout) and 07RX (lemma-equivalence-categories-schemes-over-pushout-flat), etale case; affine input Tag 08KQ(5).

proof.text: Take any affine $P_0=\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq P$ and affine $Z_0=\operatorname{Spec}E\subseteq Z$ mapping into $P_0$. By [lem-sfb-infinitesimal-pushout-affine-charts], their inverse-image charts have rings $B,A',A$ and $D,C',C$, with $R=B\times_A A'$, $C=D\otimes_BA=C'/IC'$ and $E=D\times_CC'$, all as algebras with their structural maps. The restrictions $X_0\to S_0$ and $Y_0\to T^+_0$ are etale: their inclusions into the original sources and targets are open immersions, hence etale by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-etale], so the commutative-square assertion of [lem-sfb-scheme-etale-source-target-properties] applies. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-ring-map-iff-etale-affine], $B\to D$ and $A'\to C'$ are etale. Apply [lem-sfb-fibre-product-algebra-etale] to conclude $R\to E$ is etale, hence $Z_0\to P_0$ is etale by the same affine criterion.

source.place: Tags 07RV (lemma-equivalence-categories-schemes-over-pushout) and 07RX (lemma-equivalence-categories-schemes-over-pushout-flat), etale case; affine input Tag 08KQ(5).

proof.text: Every point of $Z$ lies in a pair $Z_0\to P_0$ as in Step 3: choose an affine neighbourhood $P_0$ of its image and an affine neighbourhood $Z_0$ inside its inverse image, using [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis]. The inclusions $P_0\to P$ and $Z_0\to Z$ are etale by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-etale]. Apply (i) of [lem-sfb-scheme-etale-source-target-properties] to $Z_0\to P_0$ and $P_0\to P$ to see that $Z_0\to P$ is etale. Its jointly surjective-family assertion, for this open covering of $Z$, gives that $Z\to P$ is etale. Thus $G$ restricts to the required etale categories.

source.place: Tags 07RV (lemma-equivalence-categories-schemes-over-pushout) and 07RX (lemma-equivalence-categories-schemes-over-pushout-flat), etale case; affine input Tag 08KQ(5).

proof.text: The two canonical maps $X\to Z\times_PS$ and $Y\to Z\times_PT^+$ are isomorphisms by [lem-sfb-infinitesimal-pushout-affine-charts]. They form the adjunction unit from Step 2: each is the pair of the pushout inclusion and its structural map. On $U$ their projections to $Z$ coincide by the pushout relation and their projections to $T$ coincide by $\phi$; uniqueness in [def-pc-fibre-product] proves compatibility with $\phi$. For a morphism of triples, both sides of the naturality equation have these same projections, so the unit is a natural isomorphism.

source.place: Tags 07RV (lemma-equivalence-categories-schemes-over-pushout) and 07RX (lemma-equivalence-categories-schemes-over-pushout-flat), etale case; affine input Tag 08KQ(5).

proof.text: For an etale $W\to P$, flatness is part of [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Therefore [lem-sfb-scheme-pushout-flat-patching] identifies the canonical map $G(F(W))\to W$ with an isomorphism. It is the adjunction counit from Step 2 because its restrictions are the two projections to $W$. For a map $W\to W_1$, the naturality equation holds after restriction to both pushout components, hence holds by pushout uniqueness. The natural unit and counit isomorphisms give mutually quasi-inverse functors, including the claimed pushout description of every $W$. None of the cited statements requires quasi-compactness, separation or a uniform nilpotence exponent.
